functions.name: manif::average_biinvariant
functions.signature:
template <template <typename LieGroup, typename... Args> class Container, typename LieGroup, typename... Args>
LieGroup manif::average_biinvariant(const Container<LieGroup, Args...>& points,
                                    typename LieGroup::Scalar eps = Constants<typename LieGroup::Scalar>::eps,
                                    int max_iterations = 20)
functions.description: Compute a bi-invariant average (mean) of a set of ‘close’ Lie group elements using an iterative update of the current average by the mean of right-invariant increments. Stops when the update norm falls below eps or when max_iterations is reached. Typical use: averaging poses/transformations on a Lie group when samples are close.
requirements: points must not be empty (enforced by MANIF_CHECK).
If points contains exactly one element, that element is returned unchanged.
Input elements should be ‘close’ on the manifold to ensure convergence (stated in the documentation comment).
Container must hold LieGroup elements and support begin(), end(), size(), empty(), and iteration.

LieGroup must define types Scalar and Tangent, and support: subtraction of two LieGroup elements yielding a Tangent (operator- or equivalent), addition of a Tangent to a LieGroup (group plus, operator+=), Tangent::setZero(), Tangent::coeffs().squaredNorm().
eps is a non-negative threshold used on the squared norm of the update; choose > 0 to allow termination.
max_iterations should be a positive integer (>= 1).

functions.name: manif::average
functions.signature:
template <template <typename LieGroup, typename... Args> class Container, typename LieGroup, typename... Args>
LieGroup manif::average(const Container<LieGroup, Args...>& points,
                        typename LieGroup::Scalar eps = Constants<typename LieGroup::Scalar>::eps,
                        int max_iterations = 20)
functions.description: Compute an average of Lie group elements via an iterative, Jacobian-weighted scheme. At each iteration, it accumulates weighted log ‘between’ increments using right Jacobians and updates the average. Terminates when a derived quadratic form of the update falls below a threshold or when max_iterations is reached. Use to average nearby poses while accounting for local curvature via right Jacobians.
requirements: points must not be empty (enforced by MANIF_CHECK).
If points contains exactly one element, that element is returned unchanged.
Container must hold LieGroup elements and support begin(), end(), size(), empty(), and iteration.

LieGroup must define types Scalar, Tangent, and Jacobian, and support: avg.between(x) returning a LieGroup difference; .log() yielding a Tangent; Tangent::rjac(); Jacobian ops including transpose and multiplication; addition of a Tangent to a LieGroup (avg += ts); Tangent::setZero(); Tangent::coeffs() vector access.
eps is used as a threshold on n = ts.coeffs().transpose() * (ts.rjac().transpose()*ts.rjac()) * ts.coeffs(); choose eps >= 0, typically > 0.
max_iterations should be a positive integer (>= 1).
Elements should be reasonably close on the manifold to promote convergence (inferred from iterative local linearization).

functions.name: manif::average_frechet_left
functions.signature:
template <template <typename LieGroup, typename... Args> class Container, typename LieGroup, typename... Args>
LieGroup manif::average_frechet_left(const Container<LieGroup, Args...>& points,
                                     typename LieGroup::Scalar eps = Constants<typename LieGroup::Scalar>::eps,
                                     int max_iterations = 20)
functions.description: Compute the (left) Fréchet mean of Lie group elements via an iterative left-invariant update. At each step it accumulates left-invariant log residuals with the left Jacobian at the current average, then updates using the inverse left Jacobian. Stops when the left-Jacobian-weighted update norm is below eps or when max_iterations is reached. Appropriate when using left-invariant metrics.
requirements: points must not be empty (enforced by MANIF_CHECK).
If points contains exactly one element, that element is returned unchanged.
Container must hold LieGroup elements and support begin(), end(), size(), empty(), and iteration.

LieGroup must define types Scalar, Tangent, and Jacobian, and support: group minus using left-invariant difference ((*it) - avg_0) returning Tangent; .log(); Tangent::ljac() and ljacinv() called on avg_0.log(); group plus with left convention (avg = avg_0 + ...); Tangent::setZero(); Tangent::coeffs().squaredNorm().
eps is a non-negative threshold on the squared norm of tmp = avg_0.log().ljac() * (avg - avg_0); choose > 0 to enable termination.
max_iterations should be a positive integer (>= 1).
Elements should be sufficiently close for the local linearization to be valid and to aid convergence (inferred from algorithm nature).

functions.name: manif::average_frechet_right
functions.signature:
template <template <typename LieGroup, typename... Args> class Container, typename LieGroup, typename... Args>
LieGroup manif::average_frechet_right(const Container<LieGroup, Args...>& points,
                                      typename LieGroup::Scalar eps = Constants<typename LieGroup::Scalar>::eps,
                                      int max_iterations = 20)
functions.description: Compute the (right) Fréchet mean of Lie group elements via an iterative right-invariant update. It accumulates right-invariant residuals using lminus (Xi ⊖ Avg), weights them with the right Jacobian at the current average, and updates using the inverse right Jacobian via left-plus. Stops when the right-Jacobian-weighted update norm is below eps or when max_iterations is reached. Appropriate when using right-invariant metrics.
requirements: points must not be empty (enforced by MANIF_CHECK).
If points contains exactly one element, that element is returned unchanged.
Container must hold LieGroup elements and support begin(), end(), size(), empty(), and iteration.

LieGroup must define types Scalar, Tangent, and Jacobian, and support: lminus (it->lminus(avg_0)) returning Tangent; .log(); Tangent::rjac() and rjacinv() called on avg_0.log(); left-plus update avg = avg_0.lplus(...); lminus for computing avg.lminus(avg_0); Tangent::setZero(); Tangent::coeffs().squaredNorm().
eps is a non-negative threshold on the squared norm of tmp = avg_0.log().rjac() * (avg.lminus(avg_0)); choose > 0 to enable termination.
max_iterations should be a positive integer (>= 1).
Elements should be sufficiently close for the local linearization to be valid and to aid convergence (inferred from algorithm nature).

functions.name: manif::decasteljau
functions.description: Fits and evaluates a smooth curve on a Lie group using a De Casteljau-style recursive interpolation over piecewise segments. Given a discrete input trajectory of LieGroup states, it computes intermediate points between consecutive segments, returning an interpolated trajectory. Usage: provide a vector of Lie group elements (conforming to manif’s LieGroupBase interface), choose degree (number of control points per segment), set k_interp to control interpolation density, and set closed_curve=true to wrap remaining points into a final segment. Notes: The type parameter must support rminus (to compute the tangent between two states) and rplus (to retract along that tangent), and the tangent type must support scalar multiplication by double. Violations of preconditions are checked via MANIF_CHECK (assert/throw depending on build). The return length is number_of_segments * segment_k_interp, where number_of_segments = floor((N - degree) / degree) for N=trajectory.size(); for closed curves, an extra segment may be added if leftover points exist. segment_k_interp = k_interp if degree == 2, otherwise k_interp * degree.
requirements: trajectory.size() must be greater than 2.
degree must be less than or equal to trajectory.size().
k_interp must be greater than 0.
LieGroup must define a nested type alias LieGroup (i.e., typename LieGroup::LieGroup) used as the return element type.
LieGroup instances must support methods: rminus(const LieGroup&) returning a tangent type, and rplus(const Tangent&) returning a LieGroup.
The tangent type returned by rminus must support multiplication by a scalar double (operator*).
Elements in trajectory must be valid, initialized LieGroup objects.
If closed_curve is true, the function may use the first elements of trajectory to complete the last segment; callers should ensure the trajectory start and end are compatible for wrapping.
On precondition failure, MANIF_CHECK will trigger the library’s error handling (assertion/exception depending on configuration); callers should be prepared for this behavior.

functions.name: manif::binomial_coefficient
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
constexpr T manif::binomial_coefficient(const T n, const T k)
functions.description: Compute the binomial coefficient C(n,k) at compile time when possible. Uses a recursive formulation with simple optimizations (symmetry k -> n-k). Throws std::logic_error at runtime if preconditions on n and k are violated. Intended for integer-like types T; used by other interpolation utilities.
requirements: T must support comparison (>=), addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division
k must represent a non-negative value
n must satisfy n >= k
Inputs should represent integer values (the algorithm divides by k and assumes combinatorial semantics); behavior for non-integer T is unspecified
On invalid inputs (k < 0 or n < k) the function throws std::logic_error

functions.description: Compute base raised to the integer power exp using exponentiation by squaring. Tail-recursive via the carry parameter and constexpr-friendly. Intended for non-negative exponents.
requirements: exp must be >= 0 to reflect intended semantics; negative exp returns carry (default 1), which is not a meaningful power
T must support multiplication and copy construction/assignment
For large exp, intermediate products must be representable in T (no overflow/UB handling)

constexpr T manif::polynomialBernstein(const T n, const T i, const T t)
functions.description: Evaluate the Bernstein basis polynomial B_i^n(t) = C(n,i) * (1 - t)^(n - i) * t^i. Built from binomial_coefficient and ipow. Useful for Bézier and interpolation schemes.
requirements: Requires 0 <= i <= n to keep binomial_coefficient well-defined; otherwise std::logic_error may be thrown via binomial_coefficient
T must support construction from 1 (T(1)), subtraction, multiplication, and work with ipow
t is mathematically typically in [0,1], but the function does not enforce bounds

T manif::smoothing_phi(const T t, const std::size_t degree)
functions.description: Compute a smoothing/blending polynomial phi(t) of a given degree using hard-coded closed forms for degrees 1 through 4. Used in smooth manifold interpolation routines. Throws if an unsupported degree is requested.
requirements: degree must be one of {1, 2, 3, 4}; otherwise throws std::logic_error("Not implemented yet !")
T must support multiplication and addition, and construction from floating literals (e.g., T(3.), T(2.), etc.)
t can be any T; the function does not enforce a range (typical usage is t in [0,1])

functions.name: manif::interpolate_slerp
functions.signature:
template <typename _Derived, typename _Scalar>
static typename manif::LieGroupBase<_Derived>::LieGroup manif::interpolate_slerp(const manif::LieGroupBase<_Derived>& ma,
                                                                                  const manif::LieGroupBase<_Derived>& mb,
                                                                                  const _Scalar t)
functions.description: Spherical linear interpolation (SLERP)-style interpolation on a Lie group. Returns the point mc between ma and mb at parameter t, using right-plus/minus operations: mc = ma.rplus(mb.rminus(ma) * t). Enforces t in [0,1].
requirements: ma and mb must be valid elements of the same Lie group type associated with _Derived (operations rplus/rminus must be defined)
t must be within [0,1]; otherwise MANIF_CHECK triggers (throws)
_Scalar must be compatible with the group's tangent scaling (mb.rminus(ma) * t)
Underlying group operations must not throw for the given inputs
